doc.title: Jones Hank — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Early bands and the road to New York
title: Getting the Hot Lips Page job via Cleveland and Buffalo
summary: Lucky Thompson wrote that Page needed a pianist; Jones worked in Cleveland and Buffalo and joined Page at the Onyx Club after a union transfer wait.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Did Lucky Thompson have—Was he how you got to Hot Lips Page?

Lucky had worked with Lips before I got there. As a matter of fact, Lucky sent me a letter saying that Lips needed a pianist. He said that he needed a pianist within a certain length of time, let's say a year. So, within that year, I took the time to go to Cleveland to work at a place called Cedar Gardens for a while. After this Cedar Gardens I went to Buffalo to work at a bar. After that bar, I went to New York and joined Lips Page at that Onyx Club. This was after getting permission from the union to work on a steady job, of course. When you came to New York from out of town, you had to put in a transfer of papers. You want a lot to work on a steady job for at least six months, unless the leaders said that he could not do without you. That's how I got a steady job. I was fortunate.
